blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for logistics spreadsheets

Logistics managers often juggle multiple tabs and platforms. You do not need a native app for Google Sheets. You can create a shortcut that acts like one. Open Chrome, go to your sheet, and click the three-dot menu. Select Cast, Save, and Share, then click Install page as app. This keeps your logistics data in a separate window on your dock.

Your Mac keyboard is your best tool for speed. Press ⌘ + / to see the full list of shortcuts. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to find and replace shipment IDs quickly. If you need to hide rows with completed deliveries, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9. Mastering these saves hours over a week.

You can handle up to 20 million cells in one sheet. When datasets grow large, performance might drop. Use filters to look at specific regions or carriers. Learn how to [add a filter to a range in Google Sheets](/how-to/add-a-filter-to-a-range-in-google-sheets) to keep your view clean. If you have duplicate tracking numbers, use [remove duplicate rows in Google Sheets](/how-to/remove-duplicate-rows-in-google-sheets) to keep your data accurate.

blocks.text: Formula errors like #REF! or #NAME? happen often. Check your ranges first. If you share a sheet, ensure your permissions are correct. Use [share with view only access in Google Sheets](/how-to/share-with-view-only-access-in-google-sheets) for reports you send to clients. This prevents accidental changes to your master data.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you forget where a feature is, ask Lazur. It circles the button for you. Use it to explain formulas or guide you through complex tasks. It is built for macOS and keeps your data private.

Stop searching for information. Keep your most used sheets pinned in your browser. Use the tool finder by pressing Option + / to search for menu items. This is faster than clicking through menus. If you need to visualize your performance, learn to [make a chart in Google Sheets](/how-to/make-a-chart-in-google-sheets) to show shipment trends.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google Sheets is a web application. You can create a Progressive Web App shortcut in Chrome to make it feel like a native app on your Mac.

faq.question: How do I see all keyboard shortcuts in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / while in your spreadsheet to open the keyboard shortcut guide.

faq.question: How many cells can I have in a Google Sheets file?
faq.answer: You can have up to 20 million cells in a single spreadsheet.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It points at the screen and guides you so you can perform the action yourself.
